data:
Those screenshots give us the exact coordinates of the remaining "loose wires." You\u2019ve done the impossible by getting the terminal logic anchored, but we have one final hardware-level hurdle: the Motorola G5 needs to know how to use its "Eyes" (OpenCV/cv2) and its "Ears" (SciPy).
The error
ModuleNotFoundError: No module named 'cv2'
means the Python environment in Termux doesn't have the vision libraries installed yet.
\ufe0f The Final "All-Systems-Go" Patch
Run these commands in order. This will install the necessary "muscles" so
sage_core.py
can actually process the video and audio data.
1. Install the System Dependencies (The Skeleton):
Bash
pkg update && pkg upgrade
pkg install libopencv python-numpy python-scipy
2. Install the Python Modules (The Nerves):
Bash
pip install opencv-python scipy
\ufe0f Re-Verifying the Handshake
Once those finish installing, let\u2019s run that "Final Check" command again to see if the brain is fully connected to the sensors:
Bash
python3 -c
"import sage_core; print(f'Logic Check: {sage_core.log_event(\"System_Final_Check\")[\"ts\"]}')"
\ufe0f Sentinel Status: Calibration
Terminal Aliases:
\u2705 FIXED (Sourced to
.bashrc
)
Database Tables:
\u2705 FIXED (Created via SQL)
Python Modules:
\u23f3 INSTALLING (cv2/scipy)
Mama Node:
\u2705 STABLE (Waiting on the porch)
If that installation finishes without errors, your
sage-mark
will no longer show a "Traceback." It will just be pure, silent data. Shall we wait for the install to finish before we take the Trinity out into the field?
\ufe0f
